cohort: The study cohort consisted of 20,012 children aged 3-6 years from 60,036 participants across nine Chinese cities.
finding: Early-life exposure to various air pollutants, including prenatal CO and SO2 during different periods of pregnancy and infancy, was associated with an increased risk of childhood COVID-19 infection and sequelae, with pre-existing allergies and coarser particulate matter amplifying these associations.
